pr.title: Dismiss a settled change request once every model finds the head clean
pr.head: 66ae4d666ff94ccd3bb484f2f7248249db791465

summary: Projector's review loop posts each review as one GitHub account, and several models can review the same pull request under that account. On another author's pull request, a changes-requested verdict posts a real REQUEST_CHANGES review, which sets GitHub's reviewDecision, the status that blocks a merge. A later clean verdict posts only a COMMENT unless review.allow_approve is on, and a COMMENT replaces nothing. So the pull request stayed at CHANGES_REQUESTED after the head was found clean, and fix-pr kept reporting a change request that no finding backed.

This change makes project review publish dismiss those change requests. After it posts a review on another author's pull request, it lists the account's Projector REQUEST_CHANGES reviews that are still standing. When the newest Projector verdict on the head is clean and no finding thread is open, it dismisses each one as the reviewer, then reads them back to confirm. That is the same reading a self-review uses for its draft state since #243 made the newest verdict decide, so nothing waits for another model.

This head merges main after #243 and resolves conflicts in five files, including publish. The earlier peer wait before a dismissal is gone with the rest of the old sign-off rule. All three reviews so far are listed in the history card.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Standing change request: a REQUEST_CHANGES review by the reviewer's account that nobody dismissed and no later APPROVE by the account replaced.
  • Newest verdict: the most recent Projector verdict on the head, whichever model gave it. Since #243 it alone decides a self-review's draft state.
  • Verdict marker: the <!-- projector-review v=1 … --> line that every Projector review body carries.

cards.title: What publish does on another author's pull request
cards.html:
SituationResult
Newest verdict on the head is clean, no finding thread openDismisses the standing Projector change requests, another model's older one on the head included
A newer verdict requests changes, or a finding thread is openDismisses nothing
Another model is still reviewing the headDoes not wait; dismisses on the newest verdict
An APPROVE came after the change requestDismisses nothing
A change request without a verdict markerStays
GitHub refuses the dismissalExits 1 with the lock held; a rerun finishes

groups.title: Dismissal in publish
groups.kicker: How publish finds and dismisses the account's standing change requests
intro: standing_change_requests reads every review on the pull request by the reviewer's account, in order. An APPROVE clears the list, because an approval already replaces the earlier change requests in reviewDecision. Each REQUEST_CHANGES whose body carries a verdict marker joins the list. A dismissed review has the state DISMISSED, so it never appears.

publish calls it after the review is posted, and only on another author's pull request, since GitHub refuses REQUEST_CHANGES on your own. When a change request stands, publish reads the newest verdict on the head and the open finding threads, as a self-review does for its draft state. When the newest verdict is clean and no thread is open, dismiss sends each dismissal with the reviewer's token, and then lists the change requests again to confirm that none still stands. A failure raises before the start comment is deleted, so a rerun of publish finishes the job without posting a second review.

checks.text: A change request counts as Projector's only when verdict_marker finds a marker line in its body. The test for a hand-written change request that mentions the loop by name passes at this head.

The list of change requests is taken before the newest verdict is read. A change request that another model posts after that either becomes the newest verdict, which stops the dismissal, or is missing from the list, so it stays standing.

This dismisses another model's older change request on the head too, even while that model is still reviewing. That follows #243's rule that the newest verdict decides. An open finding thread from that model still holds every change request.

files.note: Prints a dismissed change request … line, and says the change requests stand when an open finding thread holds them.

groups.title: Dismissal tests
groups.kicker: Seven cases against the fake GitHub
intro: The fake GitHub in tests/test_review.py now returns each review's state, so the code can tell an approval from a change request, and answers the dismissal call by marking the review DISMISSED. DismissalTests sets up another author's pull request where claude-opus-5-5 requested changes on an earlier head.

checks.text: This test pins that a change request from gpt-5.5 on the head is dismissed while gpt-5.5 still has a live start comment there, because this review's clean verdict is newer.
